note: Additions from the bar-guide research (items 1, 2, 4, 7, 9, 11 and 13, requested Nov 13; ice machine updated).

item.t: Sanitizer tested with test strips: 3-compartment sink and sani buckets
item.d: Use the strips made for our sanitizer and check the reading against the range on its label. Remake anything that tests low or high.

item.t: Handwashing sink ready: soap, paper towels, and handwashing sign
item.d: Nothing in or blocking the sink; it is for handwashing only.

item.t: Sani bucket water changed during the shift
item.d: About every 2 hours, or sooner if it is cloudy or dirty. Keep buckets off the floor.

item.t: Pour spouts covered and sticky bottle necks wiped
item.d: Cap or cover every pour spout overnight to keep fruit flies out.

from.t: Bar mats pulled, cleaned, and cleaned under

to.t: Bar mats pulled, washed, sanitized, and cleaned under
to.d: Stand them up or hang them so they dry completely overnight; wet mats breed fruit flies.

ops.note: Any day during the month. Check each one off when it is done.

item.t: Walls behind and under the bar wiped
Tops of coolers and shelves wiped
Behind and under bar equipment cleaned
item.d: Pull equipment out where it is safe to.

item.t: Ice machine burned, cleaned, and sanitized inside; air filters cleaned
item.d: Turn the machine off and burn (melt) all the ice in the bin. Clean, then sanitize, the inside of the bin and every surface that touches ice, using the ice-machine cleaner and sanitizer and the steps in the machine's manual. Pull the air filters, rinse off the dust, let them dry, and put them back. Tell the MOD about any mold, slime, or damage. The full machine service still follows the manufacturer's schedule (usually every 6 months).
